chunks: From Safwan al-Jammal, he said: I heard him saying:

Whenever two believers meet and shake hands, the more faithful of them is the one who loves the other more. And no two believers ever meet, shake hands, remember Allah, and then part, except that Allah forgives them, if Allah wills.

key_terms.أَفْضَلَهُمَا إِيمَانًا: the more faithful of the two

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of shaking hands between two believers?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this narration from *Kitab al-Mumin* underscores that physical affection like shaking hands is not merely social but a spiritual conduit for divine mercy, reflecting the high status of *mawaddah* (affection) among believers. It establishes a direct correlation between the intensity of love and the level of faith, while also highlighting the communal aspect of forgiveness achieved through mutual remembrance of Allah.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 60. It has been related that Safwan al-Jammal said: I heard him (al-Sadiq (a.s)) saying:

Whenever two believers meet and shake hands, the more faithful of them would be the one who loved the other more. And no two believers ever met, shook hands, remembered Allah and then parted except that Allah forgave them.
